title_full_ar: بيان السنة والجماعة على مذهب فقهاء الملة: أبي حنيفة النعمان وأبي يوسف يعقوب والإمام محمد بن الحسن الشيباني
subject: aqeedah
summary: Al-Aqida al-Tahawiyya is the concise creedal text by Imam Abu Ja'far al-Tahawi al-Hanafi (d. 321 AH / 933 CE), presenting the beliefs of Ahl us-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah in 113 brief statements. It is one of the most authoritative and universally accepted doctrinal texts across the Sunni tradition, studied in Islamic institutions worldwide and the subject of multiple classical commentaries.
overview:
Al-Aqida al-Tahawiyya by Imam Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tahawi al-Hanafi (239–321 AH / 853–933 CE) is the most celebrated and widely studied creedal text in the Sunni tradition. Al-Tahawi was a leading Hanafi jurist and hadith scholar of Egypt whose scholarly lineage included his maternal uncle Imam al-Muzani, a student of Imam al-Shafi'i. Despite his Hanafi affiliation, his creedal text is accepted across all four madhabs as an authoritative statement of mainstream Sunni belief.

The text consists of 113 brief declarative statements covering all the major articles of Islamic faith: the oneness of God (tawhid) and His attributes, the angels, divine books, the prophets and messengers, the Day of Resurrection, divine decree (qadar), the nature of faith (iman), the position of the Companions, the legitimacy of the first four caliphs, and the conditions for intercession. The statements are phrased with precision and economy, deliberately avoiding the speculative theology (kalam) debates that divided Muslim scholars while affirming the foundational beliefs.

Al-Tahawi explicitly aligns his creed with 'the madhab of the people of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl us-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah) on the school of the jurists of the Islamic community: Abu Hanifa al-Nu'man, Abu Yusuf Ya'qub, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shaybani.' Despite this Hanafi framing, the doctrinal content is broadly accepted by all four schools.

The text attracted major scholarly commentaries: the most celebrated is Sharh al-Aqida al-Tahawiyya by Ibn Abi al-Izz al-Hanafi (d. 792 AH), a commentary extensively endorsed by Ibn Taymiyyah's school and widely used in Salafi educational contexts. It should be noted that some scholars have raised questions about aspects of Ibn Abi al-Izz's commentary that go beyond al-Tahawi's own positions. Other commentaries include those by Ibn al-Turkumani and contemporary explanations by Shaykh Shu'ayb al-Arnaut.

The text is memorised by students of Islamic theology across the Sunni world and is used as an introductory creed text in traditional Islamic institutions in the Arab world, South Asia, and beyond.
structure: 113 doctrinal statements; commonly published in 1 volume with various commentaries
